_about: Nerd facts for Cities and Capitals cards (the 🤓 Nerd facts pop-up). Keyed by card id. Each fact: [label, text], kid-friendly, 160 characters max.
_verify: Written from memory on 2026-11-19. Fact-check before launch.

rio: The Christ the Redeemer statue looks over Rio from the top of Corcovado mountain.
Rio's Carnival parades feature samba schools with thousands of dancers each.
Rio hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics, the first ever in South America.
new-york: The Empire State Building has its own zip code, 10118, and its lights change colors for holidays.
New York-style pizza is famous for huge, thin slices you fold in half to eat.
New York is called 'the city that never sleeps' because its subway runs all day and all night.
los-angeles: The giant Hollywood sign first said 'Hollywoodland' when it went up in 1923.
Disneyland, the first Disney theme park, opened just outside LA in 1955.
Los Angeles means 'the angels' in Spanish.
chicago: The world's first skyscraper, the Home Insurance Building, went up in Chicago in 1885.
Chicago is famous for deep-dish pizza, baked in a tall pan like a pie.
Every St. Patrick's Day, Chicago dyes its river bright green.
houston: When Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969, the astronauts radioed: 'Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.'
Houston's Astrodome, opened in 1965, was the world's first domed sports stadium.
Houston is the biggest city in Texas and the fourth-biggest in the US.
miami: Miami's Little Havana neighborhood is famous for Cuban coffee, music and dominoes in the park.
Miami sits between two national parks: the Everglades and Biscayne Bay.
South Beach is lined with pastel Art Deco buildings from the 1930s.
san-francisco: San Francisco's cable cars are the only moving National Historic Landmark in the US.
Sourdough bread has been a San Francisco favorite since the Gold Rush.
Thick fog often rolls through the Golden Gate. Locals have even given it a nickname: Karl!
seattle: The first Starbucks opened at Seattle's Pike Place Market in 1971.
At Pike Place Market, fishmongers toss whole salmon through the air to each other.
On clear days, snowy Mount Rainier towers over the city.
new-orleans: New Orleans is famous for beignets, square doughnuts covered in powdered sugar.
Mardi Gras parades toss colorful beads to crowds lining the streets.
Jazz legend Louis Armstrong was born in New Orleans.
las-vegas: The Las Vegas Strip glows so brightly that it can be seen from space.
Hoover Dam, one of the biggest dams in the US, is about 30 miles away.
Las Vegas has some of the biggest hotels in the world, with thousands of rooms each.
toronto: The CN Tower was the world's tallest free-standing structure for more than 30 years.
The Toronto Raptors won the 2019 NBA title, the first team outside the US to do it.
Almost half of Toronto's people were born outside Canada, making it one of the most diverse cities in the world.
montreal: Montreal is famous for poutine, fries with cheese curds and gravy, and wood-fired bagels.
The Cirque du Soleil circus started in the Montreal area in 1984.
vancouver: Stanley Park is even bigger than New York's Central Park.
So many movies and shows are filmed here that it's nicknamed 'Hollywood North.'
Vancouver has beaches and ski slopes so close that you can do both in one day.
guadalajara: Guadalajara is known for tortas ahogadas, crusty sandwiches dunked in tomato sauce.
The Mexican Hat Dance, the national dance of Mexico, comes from this region.
Guadalajara is called the 'Pearl of the West.'
cancun: Cancún was a small fishing island until it was turned into a beach resort in the 1970s.
Cancún's underwater museum has hundreds of statues on the sea floor that grow coral.
The Mesoamerican Reef, the second-biggest barrier reef on Earth, runs along this coast.
sao-paulo: São Paulo has one of the biggest Japanese communities outside Japan, so sushi is everywhere.
Brazilian football legend Pelé played for Santos, near São Paulo, for most of his career.
São Paulo's Paulista Avenue closes to cars on Sundays for people to walk, bike and play music.
medellin: Artist Fernando Botero, famous for painting and sculpting round, puffy figures, was from Medellín.
Medellín's cable cars, the Metrocable, carry people up the steep hillsides.
Every August, Medellín's Flower Festival fills the streets with giant flower displays.
cusco: Cusco's Inca stone walls fit together so tightly that a knife blade can't slip between the stones.
Cusco sits more than 11,000 feet high in the Andes.
Cusco is the gateway to Machu Picchu, the famous Inca city in the clouds.
barcelona-city: Architect Antoni Gaudí designed many of Barcelona's wavy, colorful buildings and Park Güell.
La Rambla is a famous tree-lined street full of street performers.
milan: Leonardo da Vinci's painting The Last Supper is on a wall in Milan.
Milan's cathedral, the Duomo, has more than 3,000 statues.
La Scala in Milan is one of the most famous opera houses in the world.
venice: Venice's gondolas are always painted black, and gondoliers steer them with a single oar.
The Venice Carnival is famous for its fancy masks.
Explorer Marco Polo, who traveled to China in the 1200s, came from Venice.
munich: Munich's Glockenspiel clock has life-size figures that dance and spin every day.
Bayern Munich is Germany's most successful football club.
BMW cars are made in Munich, and the company's headquarters is shaped like four car cylinders.
istanbul: The Hagia Sophia, with its giant dome, was built about 1,500 years ago.
The Grand Bazaar is one of the oldest and biggest covered markets in the world, with thousands of shops.
Simit, a ring of bread covered in sesame seeds, is sold on Istanbul street corners.
st-petersburg: The Hermitage Museum has about 3 million artworks and objects, and cats help guard it from mice!
In early summer, it's light almost all night long. These are called the White Nights.
The city has so many canals and bridges that it's called the 'Venice of the North.'
manchester: Manchester is home to two giant football clubs, Manchester United and Manchester City.
The first computer to store a program in its memory ran in Manchester in 1948.
Famous bands like Oasis started in Manchester.
liverpool-city: The Royal Liver Building has two giant bird statues, the Liver Birds, watching over the river.
Liverpool is home to two Premier League clubs, Liverpool and Everton.
The Beatles first played at the Cavern Club, a little cellar music club.
geneva: Geneva's Jet d'Eau fountain shoots water about 460 feet into the air.
The Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863.
Geneva is famous for fine watchmaking.
marseille: Marseille is the home of bouillabaisse, a fish stew with lots of herbs.
Marseille's Old Port has been a busy harbor for about 2,600 years.
France's national anthem is called 'La Marseillaise' after singers from Marseille.
dubai: Dubai has an indoor ski slope inside a shopping mall in the desert.
The Palm Jumeirah is a giant man-made island shaped like a palm tree.
Dubai's police have super-fast sports cars in their patrol fleet.
mumbai: Mumbai's dabbawalas deliver about 200,000 home-cooked lunches every day, almost never mixing one up.
The Gateway of India, a giant stone arch, stands on Mumbai's waterfront.
Cricket is everywhere: kids play on beaches, streets and fields all over Mumbai.
shanghai: Shanghai's maglev train floats above its track on magnets, with no wheels touching the rails.
The Shanghai Tower is the tallest building in China.
The Bund is a famous riverside walk lined with grand old buildings.
hong-kong: Hong Kong has the world's longest outdoor covered escalator system, carrying people up a hill.
Every night, the Symphony of Lights show makes the skyline flash with lasers and lights.
Hong Kong is famous for dim sum, small dishes like dumplings and buns.
osaka: Osaka Castle is surrounded by moats and cherry trees.
Okonomiyaki, a savory pancake you can fill with almost anything, is an Osaka favorite.
Osaka has Universal Studios Japan, home to Super Nintendo World.
kyoto: Kyoto's Fushimi Inari shrine has thousands of bright orange gates lining paths up a mountain.
Kyoto's Arashiyama bamboo forest has stalks taller than houses.
sydney: People can climb to the top of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, nicknamed 'the Coathanger.'
Sydney's New Year's Eve fireworks are among the first big celebrations on Earth each year.
Bondi Beach is one of the world's most famous surfing beaches.
melbourne: Melbourne hosts the Australian Open tennis tournament every January.
Melbourne has the biggest tram network in the world.
The Melbourne Cricket Ground holds about 100,000 fans.
auckland: The Sky Tower is the tallest structure in New Zealand, and brave people jump off it on a wire.
Auckland is called the 'City of Sails' because so many people own boats.
Auckland has the biggest Polynesian population of any city in the world.
orlando: NASA's Kennedy Space Center, where rockets launch to space, is about an hour from Orlando.
Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom opened near Orlando in 1971.
Orlando is surrounded by more than 100 lakes.
johannesburg: Nelson Mandela lived on Vilakazi Street in Soweto, a street that also housed fellow Nobel winner Desmond Tutu.
Johannesburg has millions of trees, one of the biggest city forests in the world.
Johannesburg's FNB Stadium hosted the 2010 World Cup final.
lagos: Lagos is the heart of Nollywood, one of the biggest movie industries in the world.
Afrobeat music was made famous by Fela Kuti in Lagos.
Lagos is built on islands and lagoons along the Atlantic coast.
marrakesh: Jemaa el-Fnaa square fills with storytellers, musicians and food stalls every night.
The Majorelle Garden is famous for its bright cobalt-blue buildings and cactuses.
On clear days, the snowy Atlas Mountains can be seen from Marrakesh.
casablanca: The Hassan II Mosque has a minaret about 690 feet tall, one of the tallest in the world.
Casablanca is a famous 1942 movie named after the city, though it was filmed in Hollywood!
alexandria: The Lighthouse of Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Its ancient library was one of the greatest libraries in the world.
The modern Bibliotheca Alexandrina library has a giant tilted roof shaped like a sun disc.
karachi: Karachi's colorful trucks and buses are painted with flowers, birds and patterns.
Clifton Beach is a favorite spot for camel rides by the Arabian Sea.
Karachi is famous for biryani, a spiced rice dish.
ho-chi-minh: Ho Chi Minh City has millions of motorbikes zipping through its streets.
Bánh mì, a crunchy baguette sandwich, is a famous street food here.
Its grand Central Post Office is often said to have been designed with help from Gustave Eiffel's company.
busan: Haeundae Beach is one of the most famous beaches in Korea.
Gamcheon Culture Village is a hillside neighborhood painted in rainbow colors.
The Busan International Film Festival is one of Asia's biggest movie festivals.
bangalore: Bangalore is called the 'Garden City of India' for its many parks.
India's space agency, ISRO, which sent spacecraft to the Moon and Mars, is based here.
Lalbagh Botanical Garden has a glass house modeled on London's Crystal Palace.
perth-city: Quokkas, small smiley marsupials, live on Rottnest Island, near Perth.
Perth's Kings Park is one of the biggest city parks in the world.
Perth is one of the sunniest big cities in Australia.
timbuktu: Djinguereber Mosque, made of mud and wood, was built in the 1300s.
Timbuktu was called the 'City of 333 Saints.'
People say 'from here to Timbuktu' to mean somewhere really far away.
mecca: Millions of Muslims from around the world travel to Mecca every year for the Hajj pilgrimage.
The Kaaba, a cube-shaped building covered in black cloth, stands in the center of the Great Mosque.
The Makkah Clock Tower has one of the biggest clock faces in the world.
capital-algeria: Algiers' Casbah is an old hillside neighborhood of twisting lanes and stairways, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Maqam Echahid monument has three giant concrete palm leaves rising over the city.
Algiers is one of the biggest cities on the Mediterranean coast of Africa.
capital-angola: Luanda's Fortress of São Miguel sits on a hill overlooking the bay and holds a museum.
Mussulo, a long sandy peninsula near Luanda, is a favorite beach escape.
Fish and funge, a smooth cassava dish, are favorite meals in Luanda.
capital-benin: Porto-Novo's colorful old houses mix Brazilian, African and French styles.
Porto-Novo sits on a big coastal lagoon near the Nigerian border.
The city's ethnographic museum shows traditional masks and royal objects.
capital-botswana: Gaborone was built in the 1960s to become the capital when Botswana became independent.
The Three Dikgosi Monument honors three chiefs who helped found the country.
Mokolodi Nature Reserve, near the city, protects rhinos, giraffes and cheetahs.
capital-burkina-faso: Ouagadougou hosts SIAO, one of Africa's biggest crafts fairs.
People often call the city 'Ouaga' for short.
The city has a big outdoor sculpture park with granite art by local artists.
capital-burundi: Gitega is the home of Burundi's famous royal drummers.
Gitega was the old royal capital before becoming the official capital again.
Gitega sits in green hills in the middle of the country.
capital-cabo-verde: Praia's lively music scene is full of morna and funaná songs.
Cidade Velha, near Praia, was the first town built by Europeans in the tropics.
Praia sits on Santiago, Cabo Verde's biggest island.
capital-cameroon: Yaoundé's Reunification Monument is a spiral tower you can walk up.
Mount Fébé, one of Yaoundé's hills, has views over the whole city.
Makossa, a dance music style from Cameroon, is popular in the city's clubs and radios.
capital-central-african-republic: Bangui sits on the banks of the Ubangi River, a big branch of the Congo River.
Bangui's craft markets sell carvings made from local woods.
Bangui was once nicknamed 'La Coquette,' meaning 'the pretty one.'
capital-chad: N'Djamena's Grand Mosque has tall white minarets.
The city's national museum shows ancient tools and fossils from Chad's deserts.
N'Djamena sits right on the border with Cameroon.
capital-comoros: Moroni's old Medina has narrow alleys and carved wooden doors.
The Old Friday Mosque in Moroni was first built in the 1400s.
Moroni's harbor looks out over the Indian Ocean.
capital-republic-of-the-congo: The Basilica of Sainte-Anne has a bright green tiled roof.
Brazzaville hosts FESPAM, a big festival of African music.
The Congo River rapids roar just outside the city.
capital-democratic-republic-of-the-congo: Kinshasa is the biggest French-speaking city in the world.
Lola ya Bonobo, near Kinshasa, is a sanctuary that cares for bonobos, close cousins of chimpanzees.
In 1974, Kinshasa hosted the famous 'Rumble in the Jungle' boxing match starring Muhammad Ali.
capital-ivory-coast-cote-d-ivoire: Crocodiles live in the lake around the Presidential Palace in Yamoussoukro.
Its Basilica of Our Lady of Peace was inspired by St. Peter's in Rome.
Yamoussoukro was the hometown of Ivory Coast's first president, Félix Houphouët-Boigny.
capital-djibouti: Skoudehkaris, a spiced rice and meat dish, is Djibouti's national meal.
The city's central market is full of spices, fabrics and baskets.
Djibouti City's giant port handles most of the goods going to and from Ethiopia.
capital-egypt: Cairo's Khan el-Khalili bazaar has been a busy market for more than 600 years.
Cairo is called the 'City of a Thousand Minarets.'
The Cairo Tower is shaped like a lotus flower and stands on an island in the Nile.
capital-equatorial-guinea: Malabo's cathedral has two tall towers and Gothic-style arches.
Rare monkeys like the drill live in the forests of Bioko Island, near Malabo.
Malabo's harbor sits inside the rim of an old volcano crater.
capital-eritrea: People in Asmara love cappuccinos and bicycles, a mix of local and Italian life.
Asmara sits about 7,600 feet high, so its weather stays cool.
Asmara's whole city center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
capital-eswatini: Mbabane's craft markets sell glass animals and handwoven baskets.
Mbabane is near the Ezulwini Valley, the 'Valley of Heaven.'
Mbabane grew from a trading stop on the road to Mozambique.
capital-ethiopia: Lucy, one of the most famous early human skeletons ever found, is kept in Addis Ababa's National Museum.
Merkato in Addis Ababa is one of the biggest open-air markets in Africa.
Addis Ababa sits about 7,700 feet high, one of the highest capitals in the world.
capital-gabon: Pongara National Park, across the bay, has beaches where sea turtles nest.
Libreville's St. Michael's Church is covered with carved wooden columns.
capital-gambia: Arch 22, a giant gateway with a museum on top, welcomes visitors to Banjul.
Kachikally Pool, near Banjul, has friendly crocodiles that people visit.
Albert Market in Banjul is full of colorful fabrics, fish and spices.
capital-ghana: Independence Square in Accra has a big Black Star Gate honoring Ghana's freedom.
Makola Market in Accra is one of the busiest markets in West Africa.
Labadi Beach is Accra's most popular beach.
capital-guinea: The Les Ballets Africains dance company is based in Conakry.
The Îles de Loos, small islands just offshore, are popular beach getaways.
Conakry's markets are famous for music and colorful cloth.
capital-guinea-bissau: Bissau's Carnival features giant masks and costumes from many local groups.
Bissau sits on the wide Geba River estuary.
Bissau's old Portuguese fort still stands near the waterfront.
capital-kenya: At the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust in Nairobi, rescued baby elephants are raised before returning to the wild.
Nairobi's Giraffe Centre lets visitors feed rare Rothschild giraffes face to face.
Nairobi's name comes from a Maasai phrase meaning 'cool water.'
capital-lesotho: Maseru sits on the Caledon River, right on the border with South Africa.
Maseru means 'place of red sandstone' in Sesotho.
Ponies are a common way to travel in Lesotho's mountains near the city.
capital-liberia: Providence Island in Monrovia is where many early settlers first arrived.
Waterside Market is Monrovia's biggest and busiest market.
Monrovia is one of the rainiest capital cities in the world.
capital-libya: Tripoli's Red Castle is a huge fortress by the sea that holds a museum.
Tripoli is called the 'Bride of the Sea' for its seaside setting.
Tripoli's old medina has covered markets selling copper, gold and fabrics.
capital-madagascar: The Rova, a royal palace complex, sits on the highest hill of Antananarivo.
People call the city 'Tana' for short.
Lemurs live at Lemurs' Park, a short drive from the city.
capital-malawi: The Lilongwe Wildlife Centre rescues and cares for injured wild animals.
Lilongwe's Old Town market sells carvings and crafts.
capital-mali: Bamako's Martyrs' Bridge crosses the wide Niger River.
Bamako's National Museum has beautiful masks and textiles.
Bamako is famous for musicians like Amadou and Mariam.
capital-mauritania: At Nouakchott's fishing beach, hundreds of colorful wooden boats come in each afternoon.
Nouakchott was built as the new capital around 1960.
Sand dunes from the Sahara reach the edges of the city.
capital-mauritius: Port Louis's Caudan Waterfront has a street of colorful umbrellas floating above it.
Port Louis has a Chinatown and markets with food from India, China, Africa and France.
Pieter Both mountain near Port Louis has a giant balancing rock on top.
capital-morocco: Rabat's Kasbah of the Udayas is a blue-and-white old neighborhood overlooking the ocean.
Rabat's Mausoleum of Mohammed V has guards in bright uniforms.
Rabat has been a royal city for more than 800 years.
capital-mozambique: Maputo's train station is one of the most beautiful in the world, with a green dome.
Maputo is famous for giant prawns and peri-peri chicken.
Maputo's old fortress, built of red stone, stands near the bay.
capital-namibia: Windhoek's Christuskirche church looks like a gingerbread house.
Windhoek mixes Namibian and German traditions, with some street names in German.
Windhoek is ringed by hills and natural hot springs.
capital-niger: Niamey's Grand Market is one of the biggest markets in West Africa.
Hippos sometimes swim in the Niger River near Niamey.
The Kennedy Bridge crosses the Niger River in Niamey.
capital-nigeria: Abuja's National Mosque has a golden dome and four tall minarets.
Abuja was built in the 1980s in the middle of Nigeria.
Aso Rock, a huge granite rock, rises behind Abuja's government buildings.
capital-rwanda: Kigali is spread across rolling green hills.
Kigali's Inema Arts Center shows paintings by local artists.
Kigali's car-free zone in the city center is a favorite place to walk.
capital-sao-tome-and-principe: São Tomé's colorful colonial buildings line its seaside avenue.
Chocolate made from local cocoa is sold all around the city.
The equator passes just south of the island, at Ilhéu das Rolas.
capital-senegal: Dakar's seaside Corniche road has outdoor gyms where people work out by the ocean.
Dakar's colorful 'car rapide' minibuses are painted with eyes and flowers.
Sandaga Market is one of Dakar's busiest markets, full of fabrics and music.
capital-seychelles: Victoria's Sir Selwyn Selwyn-Clarke Market sells fresh fish, spices and tropical fruit.
Victoria sits on Mahé, the biggest island of the Seychelles.
Giant tortoises live at the botanical garden in Victoria.
capital-sierra-leone: Freetown's Cotton Tree was a giant, centuries-old symbol of the city.
Freetown's beaches, like Lumley Beach, stretch along the Atlantic.
Fourah Bay College in Freetown, opened in 1827, is one of the oldest universities in West Africa.
capital-somalia: Lido Beach is Mogadishu's favorite seaside spot.
Mogadishu's old buildings mix Somali, Arab and Italian styles.
Bakara Market is Mogadishu's biggest market.
capital-south-africa: The Union Buildings, the president's offices, sit on a hill with big terraced gardens.
A giant 30-foot statue of Nelson Mandela stands at the Union Buildings.
capital-south-sudan: Juba is one of the fastest-growing cities in Africa.
The Nile flows right past the city.
Konyo Konyo market is one of Juba's busiest markets.
capital-sudan: Tuti Island sits right where the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet.
Khartoum's name may mean 'elephant's trunk,' after the shape where the rivers join.
The National Museum has ancient temples rescued from rising Nile waters.
capital-tanzania: Dodoma was chosen as the new capital in 1973 because it's in the middle of the country.
Dodoma sits on a dry, high plateau.
capital-togo: Lomé's Independence Monument stands in a big square downtown.
Lomé's beaches are lined with tall coconut palms.
Lomé is right on the border with Ghana.
capital-tunisia: The Bardo Museum in Tunis has one of the world's biggest collections of Roman mosaics.
Tunis's old medina has more than 700 historic buildings.
Tunis sits beside a big lake that opens to the Mediterranean.
capital-uganda: Namirembe Cathedral sits on top of one of Kampala's hills, with views over the whole city.
Owino Market is one of the biggest markets in East Africa.
Boda-bodas, motorbike taxis, zip around Kampala's hills.
capital-zambia: Lusaka was planned as the capital in the 1930s.
Lusaka's Sunday craft market fills a parking lot with carvings and fabrics.
Lusaka National Park, close to the city, has rhinos and giraffes.
capital-zimbabwe: Harare's Balancing Rocks, piles of giant boulders, are on Zimbabwe's money.
The National Gallery of Zimbabwe in Harare shows famous stone sculptures.
capital-afghanistan: Kabul sits in a valley surrounded by the Hindu Kush mountains.
Kite flying is a hugely popular pastime in Kabul.
Kabul has been a stop on trade routes for more than 3,000 years.
capital-armenia: The Cascade in Yerevan is a giant stairway of fountains and gardens with art museums inside.
Yerevan was founded in 782 BC, so it's older than Rome.
Yerevan's Matenadaran holds thousands of ancient handwritten books.
capital-azerbaijan: Baku's old walled city has the Maiden Tower, which is about 900 years old or older.
Baku is the lowest-lying capital in the world, below sea level by the Caspian Sea.
Baku's carpet museum is built in the shape of a rolled-up carpet.
capital-bahrain: The Bahrain World Trade Center has three giant wind turbines between its two towers.
Bahrain's pearling trail in Muharraq is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Manama's Bab Al Bahrain gate leads into a busy old market.
capital-bangladesh: Bangladesh's National Parliament building in Dhaka, by architect Louis Kahn, is famous for its giant geometric shapes.
Dhaka hosts a giant book fair every February.
Dhaka sits beside the Buriganga River.
capital-bhutan: Instead of traffic lights, police officers direct traffic in Thimphu with graceful hand signals.
A giant golden Buddha statue sits on a hill overlooking Thimphu.
Thimphu has a preserve for the takin, Bhutan's national animal.
capital-brunei: The Royal Regalia Museum holds a golden chariot used in royal parades.
Proboscis monkeys, with big long noses, live in the mangroves near the city.
Water taxis zip across the Brunei River all day long.
capital-cambodia: Phnom Penh's Central Market is a giant yellow Art Deco dome.
During the Water Festival, colorful dragon boats race on the river.
Phnom Penh means 'Penh's Hill,' after a woman named Penh who founded a temple there.
capital-china: Tiananmen Square is one of the biggest city squares in the world.
The Temple of Heaven is where emperors once prayed for good harvests.
Beijing is the only city to host both the Summer and Winter Olympics, in 2008 and 2022.
capital-georgia: A cable car carries visitors over Tbilisi to the old Narikala Fortress.
The Bridge of Peace is a curvy glass-and-steel bridge that lights up at night.
Tbilisi's old town is full of houses with carved wooden balconies.
capital-india: The Lotus Temple in New Delhi is shaped like a giant white lotus flower.
Delhi's Chandni Chowk market is one of the oldest and busiest in India.
Qutub Minar in Delhi is one of the tallest brick towers in the world, built in the 1200s.
capital-indonesia: Jakarta's Old Town, Kota Tua, has a square lined with Dutch colonial buildings.
The Istiqlal Mosque is one of the largest mosques in Southeast Asia.
Indonesia is building a new capital, Nusantara, on the island of Borneo.
capital-iran: The Azadi Tower is a white marble gateway that welcomes people to Tehran.
Tehran's Grand Bazaar has miles of covered lanes full of shops.
The National Jewelry Treasury in Tehran holds the Darya-ye Noor, one of the biggest pink diamonds.
capital-iraq: The Tigris River flows right through the middle of Baghdad.
Al-Mutanabbi Street is Baghdad's famous book-market street.
Masgouf, fish slow-roasted beside an open fire, is a Baghdad specialty.
capital-japan: Tokyo Skytree, about 2,080 feet tall, is the tallest tower in the world.
Tokyo's trains are so on time that a train company once apologized for leaving 20 seconds early!
Tokyo has more Michelin-starred restaurants than any other city.
capital-jordan: Amman's Habibah sweet shop is famous for knafeh, a cheesy, syrupy dessert.
The Citadel, on Amman's highest hill, has a giant stone hand from an ancient statue.
Rainbow Street in Amman is lined with cafés and art shops.
capital-kazakhstan: Khan Shatyr is a giant see-through tent with an indoor beach inside.
Astana is one of the coldest capital cities in the world.
Astana's name simply means 'the capital' in Kazakh.
capital-kuwait: Souq Al-Mubarakiya is one of Kuwait's oldest markets, famous for dates and spices.
The Liberation Tower is one of the tallest telecom towers in the world.
The Kuwait Scientific Center has an aquarium with a giant shark tank.
capital-kyrgyzstan: Osh Bazaar in Bishkek is full of dried fruit, nuts and felt crafts.
Ala Archa National Park, with glaciers and snowy peaks, is just outside the city.
The giant statue of Manas, the hero of Kyrgyz legend, stands in the city.
capital-laos: Patuxai is a big victory gate in Vientiane, with a viewing deck on top.
Every evening, a night market fills the Mekong riverbank.
Buddha Park, near Vientiane, has more than 200 giant concrete statues.
capital-lebanon: Pigeon Rocks are two giant rock arches standing in the sea off Beirut.
Beirut is famous for mezze, many small dishes like hummus and tabbouleh shared together.
The National Museum of Beirut has ancient treasures from many civilizations.
capital-malaysia: The Batu Caves, near Kuala Lumpur, have a giant golden statue and 272 rainbow-painted steps.
Kuala Lumpur means 'muddy river mouth' in Malay.
The KL Tower has a glass box on top where visitors seem to float in the sky.
capital-maldives: Malé is linked to the airport island by the China-Maldives Friendship Bridge.
Malé's Old Friday Mosque is built from coral stone carved by hand.
Malé is one of the most crowded cities in the world, packed onto about 3 square miles.
capital-mongolia: A giant silver statue of a horseman stands outside Ulaanbaatar.
Many families on the edge of the city live in round felt tents called gers.
Gandan Monastery has a statue more than 80 feet tall inside.
capital-myanmar: Uppatasanti Pagoda in Naypyidaw is almost the same height as Yangon's famous Shwedagon Pagoda.
Naypyidaw has a big zoo with a penguin house kept cool year-round.
capital-nepal: Kathmandu's Kumari is a girl honored as a living goddess.

Indianapolis has the biggest children's museum in the world.
The winner of the Indy 500 drinks milk to celebrate, a tradition since 1936.
state-capital-iowa: The State Capitol in Des Moines has a gold dome covered in real gold leaf.
Iowa grows more corn than almost any other state.
Des Moines' Pappajohn Sculpture Park is full of giant modern art.
state-capital-kansas: Topeka's Brown v. Board of Education case led to the end of school segregation in 1954.
Kansas grows more wheat than almost any other state, earning the nickname 'Breadbasket of America.'
A statue called Ad Astra, an archer aiming at the stars, stands on top of the Capitol dome.
state-capital-kentucky: Frankfort's Capitol has a giant floral clock made of thousands of plants.
Kentucky is famous for the Kentucky Derby horse race, held in Louisville.
Frankfort sits in a curvy bend of the Kentucky River.
state-capital-louisiana: Louisiana is famous for gumbo, jambalaya and crawfish.
Swamps near Baton Rouge are home to alligators and herons.
Baton Rouge is home to LSU and its live tiger mascot, Mike.
state-capital-maine: Augusta's Old Fort Western is the oldest wooden fort still standing in the US, built in 1754.
Maine is the first place in the US to see the sunrise for much of the year.
Maine's capitol dome is topped by a statue called Wisdom.
state-capital-maryland: Annapolis is often called the 'Sailing Capital of the World.'
Maryland's State House is the oldest state capitol still used by lawmakers.
Maryland is famous for blue crabs, often steamed with spicy seasoning.
state-capital-massachusetts: Boston's Freedom Trail is a red-brick line that leads to 16 historic sites.
The first public school in America, Boston Latin School, opened in 1635.
The Boston Marathon is the world's oldest yearly marathon, first run in 1897.
state-capital-michigan: Lansing is home to Michigan State University, the Spartans.
Michigan is the only state made of two peninsulas.
Lansing's R.E. Olds Transportation Museum shows early cars built in the city.
state-capital-minnesota: Saint Paul's Cathedral is one of the biggest churches in the US.
Minnesota is famous for the 'Juicy Lucy,' a burger with melted cheese inside.
Charles Schulz, creator of Peanuts and Charlie Brown, grew up in Saint Paul.
state-capital-mississippi: Author Eudora Welty lived in Jackson, and her house is now a museum.
The Mississippi River gives the state its name.
Jackson hosts the Mississippi State Fair every October.
state-capital-missouri: Missouri's Capitol has giant murals by artist Thomas Hart Benton.
The Gateway Arch in St. Louis, Missouri, is the tallest arch in the world.
The Katy Trail, a long bike path, passes near Jefferson City.
state-capital-montana: Helena is near the Gates of the Mountains, a canyon on the Missouri River named by Lewis and Clark.
Helena's Cathedral of St. Helena has twin spires modeled on a church in Vienna.
Bighorn sheep and mountain goats live in the mountains around Helena.
state-capital-nebraska: The Reuben sandwich and Kool-Aid both come from Nebraska.
Lincoln is home to the University of Nebraska Cornhuskers, whose stadium fills with red-clad fans.
Every spring, about a million sandhill cranes stop along Nebraska's Platte River.
state-capital-nevada: Nevada's Capitol has a silver-colored dome, honoring the state's silver mining.
Lake Tahoe, a deep blue mountain lake, is a short drive from Carson City.
Carson City's old mint once made US coins from Nevada silver.
state-capital-new-hampshire: New Hampshire holds the first presidential primary election in every election year.
Concord's McAuliffe-Shepard Discovery Center is a space museum with a planetarium.
Mount Washington in New Hampshire has some of the strongest winds ever measured.
state-capital-new-jersey: Thomas Edison made his famous light bulb and the phonograph at his lab in Menlo Park, New Jersey.
New Jersey is called the Garden State and is famous for blueberries and tomatoes.
Trenton's capitol dome is covered with gold leaf.
state-capital-new-mexico: Santa Fe's Palace of the Governors is the oldest public building in the US still in use.
New Mexicans love green and red chile; ask for 'Christmas' to get both!
Santa Fe's capitol is round, and it's nicknamed the 'Roundhouse.'
state-capital-new-york: New York's Capitol in Albany has a famous 'Million Dollar Staircase.'
The Empire State Plaza has a giant egg-shaped concert hall called 'the Egg.'
Albany sits on the Hudson River, which flows down to New York City.
state-capital-north-carolina: The Wright brothers made the first airplane flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.
Raleigh is part of the Research Triangle, a big center for science and technology.
Raleigh drops a giant acorn on New Year's Eve, like New York's ball drop.
state-capital-north-dakota: North Dakota's Capitol is a tall Art Deco tower nicknamed the 'Skyscraper of the Prairie.'
Sakakawea, who guided Lewis and Clark, has a statue at the Capitol.
Bismarck hosts a big powwow each September with dancers from many tribes.
state-capital-ohio: Columbus has the German Village, a neighborhood of old brick houses and streets.
Ohio has produced more astronauts than almost any other state, including Neil Armstrong and John Glenn.
Columbus hosts the Arnold Sports Festival, one of the biggest sports festivals in the world.
state-capital-oklahoma: Oklahoma City's Myriad Botanical Gardens has a tube-shaped greenhouse full of tropical plants.
Oklahoma City's Bricktown has a canal with water taxis.
The Oklahoma City Thunder won the NBA title in 2025.
state-capital-oregon: Silver Falls State Park, near Salem, has a trail that goes behind waterfalls.
Salem's Riverfront Carousel has horses carved by local volunteers.
Oregon is famous for hazelnuts, berries and Christmas trees.
state-capital-pennsylvania: Hershey, Pennsylvania, nicknamed 'Chocolatetown,' is a short drive from Harrisburg.
The Pennsylvania Farm Show in Harrisburg is the biggest indoor farm show in the US.
The Walnut Street Bridge lets people walk across the Susquehanna River.
state-capital-rhode-island: Rhode Island is the smallest state in the US.
Rhode Island's State House has one of the biggest self-supporting marble domes in the world.
Providence is home to Brown University and the Rhode Island School of Design.
state-capital-south-carolina: Riverbanks Zoo in Columbia has gorillas, koalas and an aquarium.
Congaree National Park, near Columbia, has some of the tallest trees in the eastern US.
Columbia is home to the University of South Carolina Gamecocks.
state-capital-south-dakota: Pierre sits on the Missouri River near Lake Oahe, a giant reservoir.
Bison roam the wide grasslands around Pierre.
Pierre is pronounced 'peer,' not like the French name.
state-capital-tennessee: Nashville has a full-size copy of the ancient Greek Parthenon, with a giant statue of Athena.
The Grand Ole Opry, a famous country music radio show, has run since 1925.
Nashville hot chicken is fried chicken coated in spicy pepper paste.
state-capital-texas: The Texas Capitol in Austin is taller than the US Capitol in Washington, D.C.
Austin hosts South by Southwest, a giant music, film and tech festival.
state-capital-utah: Five national parks are a few hours' drive from Salt Lake City, including Arches and Zion.
Utah eats more Jell-O per person than almost any other state.
Ski resorts are less than an hour from downtown Salt Lake City.
state-capital-vermont: Ben & Jerry's ice cream was started in Vermont in 1978.
Montpelier's capitol dome is covered in gold leaf, with a statue of the goddess of farming on top.
Montpelier is the only state capital without a McDonald's.
state-capital-virginia: Richmond's Capitol was designed by Thomas Jefferson.
Virginia is called the 'Mother of Presidents' because eight presidents were born there.
Richmond's Maymont park has a petting farm, gardens and wildlife exhibits.
state-capital-washington: Washington's Capitol in Olympia has one of the tallest masonry domes in the world.
Olympic National Park, with rainforests and glaciers, is a short drive away.
Washington grows more apples than any other state.
state-capital-west-virginia: West Virginia is called the 'Mountain State' because almost all of it is hilly or mountainous.
The New River Gorge Bridge, a long steel arch, is about an hour from Charleston.
The pepperoni roll, a bread roll baked with pepperoni inside, is West Virginia's famous snack.
state-capital-wisconsin: Madison's Saturday farmers market circles the whole Capitol Square.
Wisconsin makes more cheese than any other state.
Madison's Capitol is the tallest building in the city by law.
state-capital-wyoming: Wyoming has the fewest people of any US state.
Yellowstone, the world's first national park, is mostly in Wyoming.
Wyoming was the first state to let women vote, in 1869.
